headline: An AI Just Ran a DNA Lab for 8 Days — Humans Only Refilled the Chemicals
author: NEURAL_BLACK
text:
An AI Just Ran a DNA Lab for 8 Days — Humans Only Refilled the Chemicals

An AI just ran a DNA lab for eight days straight — and the humans only refilled the chemicals.

AutoDNA, from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, is a team of AI agents that designs experiments, writes the code, and drives more than 20 instruments. Published in Nature on November 4, 2026, its hardest test stored a sentence inside DNA — 78 strands, 11,382 robot steps, 203.5 hours — and read it back letter-perfect, zero errors. Then it found a KRAS G13D cancer mutation in a real tumor sample and built its own primers to prove it.

But it's not fully autonomous: 14 hardware errors hit the run, and 6 needed human hands. Humans still choose the question, refill the reagents, and clear the waste.

Primary source: Wu et al., "An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations", Nature, 4 Nov 2026 — https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11228-6 (preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02379)
